name: AI landing page design audit (contrast, fonts, CTA) with MiroMiro

parameters.content:
## AI landing page design audit
Paste any landing page into the form and get a design and conversion audit in your browser, with a score out of 100, the issues ranked, and quick wins.

Unlike text-only audits, it is based on the page's **real design**, measured by MiroMiro:
- **Contrast** of text and buttons, checked against WCAG
- **Consistency**: how many fonts, font sizes and colors the page uses
- **The hero**: its headline and calls to action
- **Structure**: which sections the page has, in order (trust, pricing, FAQ...)

The AI only explains and prioritizes those measurements. About 45 MiroMiro credits per audit.

**Setup (2 minutes)**
1. Get a free MiroMiro API key (300 credits a month, no card): https://miromiro.app/api/onboarding
2. Open any MiroMiro node > Credential > Create new, paste the key.
3. Add your AI model credential on **Chat model** (Anthropic here; swap in OpenAI or Gemini if you prefer).
4. Open the form: **Audit a landing page** > Test URL (or activate the workflow for a permanent link).

parameters.formDescription: Paste a landing page. MiroMiro measures its real design and AI writes the audit.

values.fieldLabel: What should this page get visitors to do?

parameters.text:
=You are a senior conversion and visual designer. Audit this landing page using ONLY the measured facts below (read from the live page by MiroMiro). Never invent numbers; when a fact is missing, say so.

Facts:
{{ $json.factsText }}

Write the audit in Markdown with exactly these parts, each starting with a "## " heading:
1. "## Score: N/100", then a one-sentence verdict.
2. "## What works" - 2 to 4 bullets.
3. "## Issues, most important first" - at most 4. For each: what is wrong, the evidence (the measured number, e.g. contrast 3.1:1 fails WCAG AA), why it costs conversions, and the fix.
   Check: contrast (WCAG AA needs 4.5:1 for text), too many font families (more than 2-3) or font sizes (a clean type scale has about 6-10), too many colors, whether the hero headline says what the product does, whether there is ONE clear primary call to action, and whether the page has trust sections (testimonials, logos, reviews), pricing or an FAQ before the footer.
4. "## Quick wins this week" - 3 numbered, concrete changes.

How to read the facts:
- sectionsInOrder holds the FIRST WORDS of each section, not its type. A quote ("You'll probably build a better product...") is a testimonial. Image-only sections, like customer logo strips, have no words and may look empty or be missing. So never state that trust content is missing: if you cannot spot it, say "trust content was not detected in the section text" and suggest checking.
- If hero.headlineNote is set, the headline is rotating text: never call it a run-on or keyword stuffing.
- Font and color counts can include ones used by embedded demos or widgets: report the counts, but only name a font as the brand's if brand.fonts lists it.
- Prefer measured contrast, type and color numbers over guesses about copy.
Write to the site owner: never mention these facts, field names or notes (say "the headline", not "headlineNote").
Keep it under 400 words. Plain, direct language.
